literature_row.qualitative_findings: Inequality and unpredictability of success both rise with social influence. 'The best songs rarely did poorly, and the worst rarely did well, but any other result was possible.' Quality (independent-condition market share) sets only loose bounds on success; luck (early social signal) governs the middle.
literature_row.relation_to_P2: Qualitative support for P2's DIRECTION in few-trial reward markets: top success is only weakly pinned by ex-ante quality. Labelled literature-based, not a measured rung.
